findings.title: Unexpected host write failures are reported as definitely not applied
trace: beginMessageSettingsEdit.apply revokes the opening and invokes onChange.
A host write may mutate C and then throw; commitMessageSettingsChange does not roll back or guarantee nonthrowing post-write notification.
The broad catch returns unavailable; UI asserts 未应用选择 even though C may have changed.
findings.request: Separate known pre-write validation failure from an unexpected host callback/write exception. Report an unconfirmed outcome truthfully and inspect current controlled value; never silently retry the same opening. Add one mutate-then-throw host regression, not only throw-before-write.

findings.title: Retained details navigation from an earlier opening can revoke the new opening
trace: Injected details renderer retains navigate callback from opening1.
Calling retained callback unconditionally invokes revoke against activeOpening2, clears its candidate and schedules old action via dialog.navigate.
findings.request: Bind details navigation to the captured opening and require it still be active and current before revoking or navigating. A retained callback after cancel/reopen must neither cancel the new session nor navigate. Keep legitimate explicit details close/focus handoff.

positiveObservations: Required opaque symbol and live synchronous host read/capture/write seam are explicit.
Apply revokes opening before host invocation, preventing repeat/reentrant commits.
Stage/filter callbacks guard current opening identity.
Choice projection is limited to currently authorized profile, avoiding old all-profile flatMap.
New UI separates applied C from local pending candidate and does not infer a tuple from independent axes.
peerReview: Panels separately identified same-visible-pane ownership-change suppressReturnFocus behavior; its fixed-copy report is independent.
scopeAndLimits: Snapshot is early, owner code continues; final target and manifest must be re-reviewed.
No imports, typecheck, direct tests, browser or service/resource sampling.
No product project writes by root.

cleanCode.scope: callback authority, explicit outcome semantics, single draft owner, narrow projection, liveness cleanup
cleanCode.result: Two concrete behavior findings, sent directly to soleowner; avoid broad new framework or public capability changes.
